boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-first sequence through named campus landmarks, a museum, and a science center; confirm current hours and event availability before setting out.

cards.title: Start with the UNC Visitors Center
cards.subtitle: Morehead Building · campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Pick up the self-guided historic-campus context here, then use it to set a walking route before exploring the nearby landmarks.
cards.short_summary: Begin with campus context and a route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide identifies the Visitors’ Center in the Morehead Building and describes recorded historic-campus tours.
cards.access_notes: Check the Visitors Center’s current tour and office availability before arrival.

cards.title: Pause at the Unsung Founders Memorial
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · memorial stop
cards.notes: Read the memorial’s interpretation and take a moment to recognize the enslaved and free people of color it honors before continuing.
cards.short_summary: A reflective stop in the historic-campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide says the Class of 2002 memorial honors enslaved and free men and women of color who helped build Carolina.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial; follow any posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Find the Caldwell Monument
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · landmark stop
cards.notes: Use the visitor-guide route to locate the white marble obelisk and connect it with Joseph Caldwell’s role as the University’s first president.
cards.short_summary: A named monument on the historic-campus route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide identifies the Caldwell Monument as a white marble obelisk at the burial site of first president Joseph Caldwell.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; visit during normal campus access periods.

cards.title: Continue to Davie Poplar
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · tree landmark
cards.notes: Stop beneath the named poplar and read the site in the context of the University’s founding story described in the visitor guide.
cards.short_summary: A historic tree landmark in the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide describes the legend that William Richardson Davie rested under this tree when selecting the University site.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; stay on surrounding paths and respect any preservation barriers.

cards.title: See the Old Well
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · university symbol
cards.notes: Make this a short photo and orientation stop, then follow the brick walks toward Old East and the rest of the historic-campus route.
cards.short_summary: The University’s visual symbol and former water source.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide calls the Old Well an unofficial University symbol and says it was one of the University’s few water sources for more than a century.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted guidance around the structure.

cards.title: Walk past Old East
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · residence hall
cards.notes: View the exterior and note its 1793 cornerstone; keep the stop outdoors because the building remains a residence hall.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark and active residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide identifies Old East as a National Historic Landmark, says its cornerstone was laid October 12, 1793, and notes it is now a residence hall.
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas; do not enter residential access areas.

cards.title: Pass South Building
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · administrative landmark
cards.notes: Take in the exterior and use the guide’s note about James K. Polk to add another chapter to the historic-campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A former dormitory that now houses University leadership offices.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide says South Building was originally a dormitory, housed James K. Polk, and now contains the chancellor’s and other administrative offices.
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas; office access may be restricted.

cards.title: Stop at Gerrard Hall
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · 1837 hall
cards.notes: Circle the building from the public walkways and use the visitor guide to place it among the long-running campus gathering spaces.
cards.short_summary: A named 1837 hall on the historic route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide states that Gerrard Hall was completed in 1837 and has been the scene of many University occasions.
cards.access_notes: Check University event scheduling before planning an interior visit.

cards.title: Spend an afternoon at the Ackland
cards.subtitle: 101 S. Columbia Street · art museum
cards.notes: Browse the galleries at your own pace, then check the current calendar for public art activities that fit the day you visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum with free public admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ackland states that admission is always free and lists its location at 101 S. Columbia Street in Chapel Hill.
cards.source_title: Visit the Ackland Art Museum at UNC-Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Regular hours listed are Wednesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; verify holiday changes.

cards.title: Close with Morehead’s exhibits or a show
cards.subtitle: Morehead Building · science-center stop
cards.notes: Choose either general-admission exhibits or a scheduled planetarium show, and reserve or buy tickets only after checking the current calendar.
cards.short_summary: A ticketed planetarium option with UNC-student admission benefits.
cards.evidence_claim: Morehead lists Tuesday–Friday, Saturday, and Sunday hours and says UNC students with a valid One Card receive free general admission and $6 show bundles.
cards.source_title: Plan A Visit - Morehead Planetarium and Science Center
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Tue–Fri 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m., Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m., and Sun 1–6 p.m.; ticketing applies to shows.
